text.p: The Casablanca stock market closed on Wednesday 0.40 percent higher with most stocks rising on an illiquid market, a stockbroker said.
The all-share index closed at 562.42 points from 560.19 points on Tuesday.
"The market illiquidity still inflates shares," a Casablanca-based broker said.
Oil refinery Samir traded unchanged at 280 dirhams with 23,624 shares changing hands.
"It has become firmer with the new trading," he added.

The exchange started last week the gradual introduction of electronic trading, with shares of four companies. ONA group, the biggest private holding, traded at 715 dirhams, unchanged for the third consecutive day.
In the banking sector, leading stock Wafabank and Banque Nationale pour le Developpement Economique were 20 and four dirhams respectively to 750 and 198 dirhams.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, Morocco's second largest conglomerate which holds diversified stakes in more than 40 firms, remained unchanged at 670 dirhams.
Brewery firm Brasseries du Maroc, unchanged from Tuesday at 1,800 dirhams had a volume of 1,300 shares.
Traded volume on the official market was 130.6 million dirhams from 85.3 million dirhams on Tuesday.
